description:
Goal
Remove readiness-probe reliance on the accidental FZ extension `test(:name), do: body`. Elixir rejects a comma after a closed parenthesized call; canonical source is either `test(:name, do: body)` or `test(:name) do ... end`. This blocks the corpus migration because the stricter ordinary-call grammar now correctly exposes the stale probes.

Signal
The existing JIT/interpreter readiness and timeout integration tests are red on the stale spelling and green on canonical syntax. An adjacent frontdoor test pins the old form as a parse error at its comma. The Elixir authority is `Code.string_to_quoted!/1`, which raises `SyntaxError` for the stale form.

Strategy
Migrate only the test-command probes to canonical keyword arguments. Preserve the general parser rejection; do not add a `test`, `def`, macro, or item-position special case.

Acceptance
Focused parser and readiness/timeout integration tests pass, the full library suite is green, and a fresh holistic reviewer confirms the change fits the Elixir-surface goal.
title: Use canonical comma-do syntax in test command probes
